newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up on wet weather, inquiries.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up on wet weather, inquiries.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended higher after inquiries from Far Eastern and European buyers and worries over the wet weather, traders said.
But demand remained weak and no significant business was reported, they said.
"The prices seem to be holding well but suppliers are shying away because of the wet weather in Bangkok and northern (Malaysian) areas," said a dealer. "So they're adjusting prices slightly."
"The demand side is still quiet," said another dealer. "If anything at all, it was marginal covering."
At the close, the MRELB quoted December RSS1 buyer at 317.50 cents ($1.53), up three cents from Thursday. December SMR 20 was a cent higher at 311.

Traders offered the SMR CV at 363, SMR L at 342, SMR 5 at 320, SMR10 at 308, SMR 20 at 307 and latex at 234. "Prices should jump five to ten percent across the board next week if the weather stays wet and demand returns," said a dealer.
The INRO five-day average rose to 242.04 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 31 from 241.03 on Oct 30. The daily indicator was higher at 244.36 against 242.83 previously.
